Here’s a concise, high-coverage profile of Francis Ngannou. Note: My latest comprehensive knowledge is current through October 2024; developments after that may not be reflected.

Identity and background
- Full name: Francis Zavier Ngannou
- Nickname: “The Predator”
- Born: September 5, 1986, in Batié, Cameroon
- Nationality: Cameroonian and French
- Size: approx. 6'4" (193 cm), reach about 83" (211 cm)
- Early life: Grew up in poverty; worked in sand mines. Migrated from Cameroon to Europe, endured homelessness in Paris before training at MMA Factory under Fernand Lopez. Later trained at Xtreme Couture with Eric Nicksick (Las Vegas).

MMA career overview
- Style/attributes: Elite knockout power (widely cited by the UFC Performance Institute for record-breaking power metrics), explosive athleticism, improved wrestling/grappling later in career.
- UFC rise (2015–2017): Stoppage wins over Curtis Blaydes, Andrei Arlovski, and a spectacular KO of Alistair Overeem (uppercut, UFC 218).
- First title shot: Lost a decision to Stipe Miocic (UFC 220, Jan 2018). Followed by a lackluster decision loss to Derrick Lewis (2018).
- Rebound KO streak (2019–2020): First-round KOs of Curtis Blaydes (rematch), Cain Velasquez, Junior dos Santos, Jairzinho Rozenstruik.
- UFC heavyweight champion: Knocked out Stipe Miocic in Round 2 to win the belt (UFC 260, Mar 27, 2021).
- Title defense: Defeated Ciryl Gane by decision (UFC 270, Jan 2022), surprising many by leaning on wrestling despite knee injuries.
- Departure from UFC: Became a free agent in early 2023 after a very public contract dispute centered on pay, sponsorship, fighter rights, and a desire to box. Was stripped of the UFC title.

Post-UFC: PFL and leadership
- Signed with the Professional Fighters League (PFL) in 2023 on a non-exclusive deal allowing boxing, equity participation, and leadership in building PFL Africa. Publicly framed as a fighter-friendly contract with minimum pay guarantees for opponents.
- As of late 2024 he had not yet returned to MMA competition since UFC 270; a targeted debut versus PFL opposition (widely linked to Renan Ferreira after PFL vs Bellator in Feb 2024) was delayed following his boxing bout with Anthony Joshua.

Professional boxing
- Debut: Tyson Fury vs Francis Ngannou, Riyadh, Oct 28, 2023. Ngannou knocked Fury down in Round 3 and lost a close split decision, earning broad respect for outperforming expectations.
- Second bout: Anthony Joshua vs Francis Ngannou, Riyadh, Mar 8, 2024. Joshua scored multiple knockdowns and won by emphatic KO in Round 2. The loss prompted a medical suspension that postponed Ngannou’s planned PFL MMA debut.
- Boxing record through 2024: 0–2 (0 KOs), with the Fury performance notably enhancing his profile despite the official loss.

Signature wins and moments (MMA)
- Alistair Overeem (KO, 2017) – iconic uppercut.
- Cain Velasquez (KO, 2019) – quick finish.
- Junior dos Santos (TKO, 2019).
- Jairzinho Rozenstruik (KO, 2020) – 20-second blitz.
- Stipe Miocic (KO, 2021) – won UFC heavyweight title.
- Ciryl Gane (UD, 2022) – first title defense.

Career stats snapshot (MMA, through 2024)
- Notable for one of the highest career knockout rates among UFC heavyweights.
- Multiple Performance of the Night bonuses.
- Regarded as one of the most dangerous punchers in MMA history.

Business, advocacy, and philanthropy
- Francis Ngannou Foundation: Builds and supports gyms and youth programs in Cameroon; opened a gym in his hometown to give local kids opportunities he lacked.
- Public stance on fighter rights: Vocal about fair pay, sponsorship freedom, long-term healthcare, and contractual flexibility; his PFL deal was cited as a model for athlete leverage.
- Role in African MMA development: Works to expand events, infrastructure, and talent pipelines across the continent (including PFL Africa initiatives).

Training and coaches
- Early MMA: MMA Factory (Paris) with Fernand Lopez.
- Later: Xtreme Couture (Las Vegas) with head coach Eric Nicksick; known to cross-train in striking and wrestling with elite partners.

Reputation and legacy
- Known for record-setting punching power, rapid ascension from extreme hardship to world champion, and shifting fighter empowerment dynamics in MMA business negotiations.
- The Fury fight, despite being a loss, became a landmark crossover moment that changed perceptions of MMA heavyweights in elite boxing settings.

What may have changed after Oct 2024
- MMA return date and opponent in the PFL.
- Any additional boxing matches, rankings, or sanctions.
- Updates to leadership roles or promotional endeavors (e.g., PFL Africa timeline).

If you’d like, I can check the latest news on his MMA return date, recent fights, or any new roles since late 2024.
